subject: sociology

moments.title: Mind, Self and Society
moments.body: Mead's lectures, published after his death, develop the I-and-me distinction and role-taking as foundations of selfhood.
moments.takeaway: The self emerges from social interaction.

moments.title: Symbolic interactionism coined
moments.body: Blumer names the tradition descended from Mead and Cooley, emphasising meanings constructed in interaction.
moments.takeaway: A name can consolidate a loose tradition.

moments.title: Symbolic Interactionism
moments.body: Blumer's book lays out the methodological principles: people act towards things on the basis of meanings they hold for them.
moments.takeaway: Methodological commitments shape what counts as data.

now.title: Interactionism today
now.body: Symbolic interactionism underpins much qualitative sociology, from microsociology to ethnography of work.
now.open_questions: How is selfhood constructed in interaction mediated by social media platforms?

reflection: American pragmatism gave sociology its strongest interactionist tradition.
